content: 1. The pharmacokinetics of nitazoxanide in patients with impaired renal or hepatic function have not been studied. Therefore, nitazoxanide should be used with caution in patients with hepatic or biliary disease, renal disease, or combined renal and hepatic disease. 2. Alinia Tablets and Alinia for Oral Suspension should be taken with food. 3. In vitro metabolism studies have shown that tizoxanide does not significantly inhibit cytochrome P450 enzymes. Although no in vivo drug-drug interaction studies have been conducted, it is expected that no significant interactions would occur when nitazoxanide is co-administered with drugs metabolized by or inhibiting cytochrome P450 enzymes. 4. Long-term carcinogenicity studies of nitazoxanide have not been conducted. 5. Nitazoxanide was not genotoxic in the Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cell chromosomal aberration assay or the mouse micronucleus assay. However, it was genotoxic in one tester strain (TA100) in the Ames bacterial mutation assay. 6. Nitazoxanide did not adversely affect male or female fertility in rats at doses of 2,400 mg/kg/day, which is approximately 20 times the clinical adult dose adjusted for body surface area. 7. Reproduction studies in rats at doses up to 3,200 mg/kg/day (approximately 26 times the clinical adult dose adjusted for body surface area) and in rabbits at doses up to 100 mg/kg/day (approximately 2 times the clinical adult dose adjusted for body surface area) revealed no evidence of impaired fertility or harm to the fetus due to nitazoxanide. However, there are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. 8. It is not known whether nitazoxanide is excreted in human milk. Because many drugs are excreted in human milk, caution should be exercised when nitazoxanide is administered to a nursing woman. 9. A single Alinia Tablet contains a greater amount of nitazoxanide than is recommended for pediatric dosing and should not be used in pediatric patients 11 years of age or younger. Alinia for Oral Suspension should be used for dosing nitazoxanide in pediatric patients. 10. The safety and effectiveness of Alinia for Oral Suspension in pediatric patients less than 1 year of age have not been studied. 11. Clinical studies of Alinia Tablets and Alinia for Oral Suspension did not include sufficient numbers of subjects aged 65 and over to determine whether they respond differently from younger subjects. In general, the greater frequency of decreased hepatic, renal, or cardiac function, and of concomitant disease or other drug therapy in elderly patients, should be considered when prescribing Alinia Tablets and Alinia for Oral Suspension. 12. As stated in the precautions section, this therapy must be administered with caution to patients with renal and/or hepatic impairment. 13. Alinia Tablets and Alinia for Oral Suspension have not been studied for the treatment of diarrhea caused by Giardia lamblia in HIV-infected or immunodeficient patients. 14. Alinia Tablets and Alinia for Oral Suspension have not been shown to be superior to placebo for the treatment of diarrhea caused by Cryptosporidium parvum in HIV-infected or immunodeficient patients.
